answers.answer: Each player starts with 25 money, 1 active association worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers below it, and draws 8 Zoo cards, keeping 4 and discarding 4. They draw 2 Final Scoring cards. All five Action cards start side I; Animals goes in slot 1 (strength 1) and the other four are randomly placed in the remaining slots. Appeal starts at 0 for the start player, then 1, 2, and 3 for the second, third, and fourth players, respectively.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C1/C3/D/E/F: '25 money'; '1 association worker' and 'remaining 3'; 'Draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4'; 'Draw 2 Final Scoring cards'; Action cards 'side I up' with Animals under the leftmost slot; Appeal staggered 0, 1, 2, 3 by turn order.

answers.answer: Four Base Conservation Project cards are placed face up below the Association board in a four-player game; otherwise three are placed (so three in a two- or three-player game). In a two-player game only, six tokens of an unused color block the left level of the left project, middle level of the middle project, right level of the right project, and all three spaces in the donation area's left column; those spaces are blocked for both players. No blocked spaces are specified for three or four players. Reveal the six-card initial display after all players have chosen their starting hands.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b: 'In a 4-player game place the 4 topmost face up ...; otherwise the 3 topmost.' Setup 5c describes the two-player blocked levels and donation spaces. Setup G: 'After everyone has chosen their hand cards, reveal the 6 cards of the display.'

answers.answer: After using the card in slot 4, remove it, shift all cards left of the empty slot one slot right, and put the used card in slot 1. Action strength is set before the action; each X-token spent adds 1 strength, and X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost that action. You may spend any number on an action, and may hold at most 5 X-tokens. An 'after finishing' effect resolves after the action is complete, including moving the Action cards.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: after completing an action, remove its card, shift cards left of the empty slot right, and place the used card in slot 1. X-token strength is set 'before performing the action'; max 5. 'After finishing' effects occur after moving the Action cards.

answers.answer: Yes. If you cannot or do not want to perform one of the five actions, take exactly 1 X-token instead. You still select an Action card, move it to slot 1, and shift the intervening cards right; strength and upgrade side do not matter. You cannot take this action while holding 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: X-TOKEN action: 'If you cannot or do not want to perform any of the 5 actions, take exactly 1 X-token'; still select and move a card to slot 1; unavailable at 5 held.

answers.answer: When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore additional movement beyond that space, and the break happens after the current turn ends. The player who reached the last space gets 1 X-token. The triggering player completes the turn; after the break, play continues clockwise with the next player. The summary does not specify a special extra-turn rule for a break trigger itself; the one-more-turn rule applies if the game end is triggered (and says all players get one more turn if that happens during a break).
answers.evidence: Break track: break 'after the end of your current turn'; gain '1 X-token'; 'Ignore any additional steps beyond the last space.' Break procedure says play continues clockwise with the next player. End of game: triggering player completes turn and others take one more; if triggered during a break, all players take one more.

answers.answer: Side I advances the Break token 2 spaces, then either draws from the deck according to the card's table (maximum 3, with a possible discard) or snaps exactly 1 display card at strength 5 or more, regardless of reputation. Side II also advances the Break token 2 spaces, then draws from the deck and/or within reputation range in any order according to its table; its snap threshold is strength 3, with no added benefit above 3. Reputation range applies to Side II display draws. Display cards are not replenished until the turn is complete, then cards shift down and empty folders refill. The hand limit is enforced only at breaks (normally 3, or 5 with the specified university).
answers.evidence: Cards action I/II specifies +2 Break movement, deck draw versus snap at 5/3, Side II deck and/or reputation range. Reputation track defines range. Special Rules: display replenished after the entire turn; hand limit only at breaks.

answers.answer: Reputation range includes the display card on the folder matching your Reputation counter and all lower-numbered folders. Reputation 10 or higher requires the upgraded Cards action. At reputation 15, each further reputation step gives 1 appeal instead. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display: 'Within reputation range' is the matching folder and lower-numbered folders; 10+ requires upgraded Cards; at 15 further reputation gives 1 appeal per step; discard pile may not be inspected.

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building whose size is no greater than the action strength. Build II builds any number of different buildings up to a total size equal to strength, but never two identical buildings in the same action. Buildings cost 2 money per space. A first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building by an edge. Build only on empty spaces, without extending off-map, overlapping, or covering water or rock. Restricted-icon spaces require upgraded Build. A kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from each other kiosk. Each pavilion immediately and once increases appeal by 1.
answers.evidence: Build action I/II gives the one-building and total-size limits and cost; Placement rules give border/adjacency, unavailable spaces, restricted icon and kiosk spacing; each pavilion gives +1 appeal once.

answers.answer: Build I offers kiosks, pavilions, standard enclosures sizes 1–5, and a size-3 Petting Zoo (maximum one per zoo). Build II additionally offers a size-5 Large Bird Aviary and size-5 Reptile House (maximum one of each per zoo). The components list has 4 Petting Zoos, 4 Reptile Houses, and 4 Large Bird Aviaries. Build cannot create unique buildings; they enter play only through Sponsor cards. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal.
answers.evidence: Build action lists buildings, sizes, maxima, unique-building restriction and full-map reward. Components list '4× Petting Zoo, 4× Reptile House, 4× Large Bird Aviary.'

answers.answer: The summary specifically says animal-play money effects pay out later, so you must be able to pay the animal's full cost before receiving that money. It does not state a general rule about using money or other bonuses gained during an action to pay for a later building or association task in that same action. Placement bonuses are taken immediately as spaces are covered; Build II says to pay for each building separately before placing it and hold 'after finishing' bonuses until the whole Build action is complete. Other non-'after finishing' animal effects resolve immediately; 'after finishing' effects wait until the action is complete and Action cards have moved. For simultaneous effects, the owning player chooses the order.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: 'must be able to pay an animal's full cost before any “gain money” effect from the play pays out.' Build II: pay for each building before placing it; placement bonuses before the next building; hold after-finishing bonuses. Animals action and Special Rules distinguish immediate/after-finishing and let the owner order simultaneous effects.

answers.answer: Before playing an animal, meet all its conditions and pay its cost. A partner zoo on the animal's continent reduces cost by 3 money per continent icon on that animal, so two such icons give a 6-money reduction. Any animal other than a Petting Zoo animal may use an empty standard enclosure at least as large as required; flip it to occupied. Some animals require adjacency to water and/or rock, and those requirements also apply when using a special enclosure. Petting Zoo animals can go only in the Petting Zoo. All reptiles and some birds can use their indicated special enclosure; mark the card's required number of spaces there with player tokens, if capacity remains, and never flip a special enclosure. Effects such as appeal/conservation/reputation resolve as specified; ordinary effects are immediate, while 'after finishing' effects wait until the whole Animals action and Action-card movement are complete.
answers.evidence: Animals action steps 1–5 specify conditions, cost discount '3 money per continent icon', enclosure size and adjacency, special-enclosure token occupancy, and effect timing.

answers.answer: Animals II permits animal cards from the display within reputation range, in addition to hand cards; pay the folder number as an additional cost. At strength 5 or more, you may increase reputation by 1 at the very beginning of the action, before using the higher range. Display cards are not replenished until the turn ends. Animals II also permits animals with upgrade-required conditions.
answers.evidence: Animals II: play from display within reputation range, pay folder number; strength 5+ reputation increases at the very beginning; no refill until turn ends; upgrade-required icon conditions allowed.

answers.answer: Existing suitable animals may move only immediately when a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary is built, once per such building. The summary allows suitable animals from standard enclosures to move but gives no numeric cap on how many; capacity is limited by the special enclosure's spaces, marked with player tokens according to the number shown for each animal. For each animal moved, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting that animal's requirements, including water/rock, back to empty. Decide separately for each animal. The summary does not specify a fallback if no suitable standard enclosure can be freed.
answers.evidence: Build II allows moving suitable animals 'immediately — and only once per building.' Special Rules: for each animal moved, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting its requirements and mark special-enclosure spaces with tokens; no fallback is stated.

answers.answer: The four task types are increase reputation, gain a partner zoo, gain a university, and conservation-project work. Their numeric strengths are not given in the summary. Side I performs exactly one task and requires action strength at least the task's strength. Side II can perform one or more different tasks whose total task value is no greater than action strength. Each task needs an active worker. If one of your workers is already on a task, you must use two workers to do it again; if three of your workers are there, you cannot do it again until after the break. Other players' workers do not matter.
answers.evidence: Association action lists four task types and the worker and side-I/II rules, including 'Other players' workers on a task do not matter.' Numeric task strength values are not stated.

answers.answer: Partner zoos and universities are taken from the Association board and placed on the lowest available spaces in the corresponding column of your zoo map; printed bonuses are taken immediately, and a university's printed reputation is advanced. You cannot take a duplicate university or a partner zoo from a continent you already have. You may have at most 4 partner zoos; the third and fourth require upgraded Association. Universities are the only way to raise the hand limit to 5; otherwise it is 3, enforced at breaks. At breaks, partner zoos and universities are replenished so each is available exactly once, except those all players already have.
answers.evidence: Association task descriptions: take from Association board to lowest empty map space, take bonuses immediately, no duplicate universities, partner zoos must be different continents and max 4 (third/fourth require upgrade); universities raise hand limit. Break procedure replenishes availability.

answers.answer: A project can be supported if already in play, or entered from hand and supported immediately during conservation-project work; Association II also allows playing it from the display within reputation range, paying the folder number. To support it, meet a condition without a player token and place one of your player tokens from the left edge of your zoo map on that condition; each player may support each project only once. The project award gives conservation and any depicted reputation. Removing the token from your map activates its bonus immediately; you choose whether to take that bonus before or after the project reward. The project row holds up to 2, 3, or 4 cards depending on player count; an overflowing project is discarded from the right, and tokens on it return to their owners' supplies, not their maps. Base projects are not moved.
answers.evidence: Association action conservation-project work and support rules describe entry, support condition/token/source, once limit, awards, bonus timing, row capacity and discarded-project token destination.

answers.answer: Yes. The animal must require a standard enclosure of the size depicted on the release project; whether it can also live in a special enclosure is irrelevant. Releasing moves your Appeal counter back by the animal's appeal value, discards the Animal card, and frees the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting its requirements, including water/rock; if releasing an animal in a special enclosure, remove the appropriate player tokens there. The summary does not specify resulting changes to counted icons, reputation, or conservation points, so those consequences are unsupported.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild: discard an Animal card with the specific icon; it 'must require a standard enclosure of the depicted size'; move Appeal back by its appeal value; flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting requirements or remove tokens from special enclosure; discard the card. No reputation or conservation changes are stated.

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly one card from hand if action strength is at least its level, after meeting its conditions; alternatively, advance the Break token by strength and take that much money, even if the token needs fewer steps to reach the last space. Sponsors II plays one or more cards if strength +1 is at least the sum of their levels (X-tokens can raise strength above 5). Cards may come from hand or from the display within reputation range, with folder number paid as an extra cost; display refill waits until turn end. Resolve cards sequentially, fully resolving each card's instant effects except 'after finishing' effects before playing the next. The break-token money option on Sponsors II pays twice the amount. Thus, if only one break step remains, the summary says Sponsors I still takes full money equal to strength and Sponsors II takes that amount twice.
answers.evidence: Sponsors I/II directly specify the level limits, display use and cost, sequential effects, and full or double money despite excess break movement.

answers.answer: Break order: discard down to hand limit (normally 3, or 5 with the particular university); return Multiplier, Venom, and Constriction tokens from Action cards; recall workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1 and 2, slide the others down and refill; take income; reset the Break token. Kiosk income is 1 money per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not count, but empty special enclosures do. Income is usually simultaneous; if effects require an order, start with the player who initiated the break (or the affected player closest to them) and proceed clockwise. Display cards taken during a turn are not replenished until the entire turn ends; then higher-numbered cards move down in order and empty spaces refill from the deck. If multiple players take display cards in the same turn, this timing still means refill happens after that turn, not between those actions.
answers.evidence: Break procedure items 1–6 provide order, hand limit, kiosk neighbors and income order. Reputation/display and Special Rules specify turn-end display refill and folder order.

answers.answer: At 2 conservation points, choose to upgrade an Action card or activate another association worker. At 5 and 8, take either 5 money or the Bonus token at that space (if available). The first time anyone reaches 10, all players discard one Final Scoring card; if nobody reaches 10 before game end, everyone discards one before scoring. The game ends whenever a player's Appeal and Conservation counters are in the same scoring area or pass one another, including if this happens during another player's turn. The triggering player finishes their turn and all other players take one more turn; if the end is triggered during a break, all players take one more turn. Each Final Scoring card can add at most 4 conservation points. Victory Points equal Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; ties go to the player with the most supported conservation projects, then are shared.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory Conditions list milestones, end trigger ('ever'), last turns, 4-point-per-card cap, VP formula and tie-break. The summary does not separately explain the timing of a trigger caused by gains during another player's turn.
